title: Prompt Economics Wizard — proto notes
content:
Quick idea log — Prompt Economics Wizard (PEW)

Context / problem
- Teams struggle to predict token costs during development: ad-hoc prompts in prod cause cost spikes.
- Current console shows aggregated cost and token breakdown per request/route, but it’s reactive. Developers need an interactive tool to estimate and optimize prompt cost before shipping.

High-level concept
- PEW = an interactive in-console and CLI assistant that estimates per-call cost, surface-cost drivers (model choice, input size, response length, n/hypotheses, temperature, reranking), and suggests low-effort optimizations (truncation, streaming thresholds, reuse of cached prefixes, model downgrades, token budgets).
- Can be used as a dev-time simulator and as a lightweight CI gate for PRs that change prompts/routes.

Primary user stories
1) As a frontend engineer, I want to paste an example user prompt + expected response length and see a breakdown of cost and latency tradeoffs across candidate models so I can pick the right model for my product tier.
2) As an ML engineer, I want PEW to run my test prompt against a historical payload distribution (sampled) and show aggregate monthly cost delta for different batching/quantization settings.
3) As a product manager, I want PEW to flag risky prompt changes (x% token increase) and add a suggested mitigation (limit response tokens, change model, add reranking) I can approve before rollout.
4) As an SRE, I want a simple exported JSON that contains the simulation configuration so we can reproduce a cost spike locally.

Core features (MVP)
- Prompt simulator UI: input prompt text, desired response max tokens, flags (streaming on/off, function-call yes/no), candidate models dropdown.
- Instant cost estimate: per-call and projected monthly cost given QPS or a small sample. Show tokens (input, output) and cost per token assumptions (hosted pricing).
- Quick optimization suggestions: "Reduce expected max tokens to N", "Use model X-small for non-critical routes", "Enable streaming after 200 tokens". Each suggestion shows estimated delta and rough latency implications.
- CI hook: simple CLI that runs against PR prompt diffs and returns a pass/fail or a cost-change badge.

Nice-to-have / v1+
- Bulk mode: run a set of sample prompts (CSV) and show percentile cost distribution.
- Integration with Optimize: automatically map suggestions to Optimize recommendations (batch size, quantization level).
- Telemetry-informed defaults: use per-customer token distribution/SLAs to simulate production.
- Opt-in auto-save as a saved "Scenario" in Console for re-use and sharing.

Low-fi flows / UI sketch (textual)
- Console > Routes > Route X > "Simulate prompt" button. Modal opens:
  - Input box: example user messages (multi-turn supported)
  - Response: expected max tokens slider (50–2000)
  - Model: dropdown (redwood-llama-70b-int8, small variants)
  - Advanced: enable streaming / function-call / n-hypotheses / reranker
  - Run -> results panel: tokens -> cost, latency estimate, suggestions listed with delta buttons.

CI CLI: pew-simulate --input example.json --model redwood-7b --qps 2 --out report.json
- returns exit code 0 if cost delta < threshold, 2 otherwise, prints short summary for GH action.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- Given an input prompt and model selection, PEW displays input/output token estimates within ±20% of runtime observed average for that model (based on a small calibration dataset).
- Suggestions show an estimated cost delta and at least one actionable optimization.
- CLI can be invoked in GH Actions and return a deterministic pass/fail for PR gating.

Telemetry and data needs
- Sample token length distributions per model (existing per-request telemetry).
- Latency profilers for model variants at representative sequence lengths.
- Pricing table reference (hosted API cost per input/output token per model).

Dependencies / integration points
- Console routes UI + API for running lightweight local simulations (no live call to expensive model by default; use cost models + small-sample calls optionally).
- Optimize service for suggestion mapping (batching/quantization recommendations).
- Attribution and billing team to validate cost formulas.

Risk & open questions
- How accurate can estimates be without invoking the full model? We need a lightweight calibration crawl or a small-sample live probe for accuracy.
- Security: Saved scenarios may contain PII. Should we mask or warn? Default to not saving by name and require explicit opt-in to persist.
- Pricing variation: customers on Dedicated/Private have different unit costs. Need mapping and per-customer config.
- Will devs rely on PEW and ignore production sampling? Make clear it’s a simulator not a guarantee; surface confidence bands.

Experiment plan (first 8 weeks)
- Week 0–1: wireframe + internal review with Console + Optimize + Billing owners.
- Week 2–3: implement simple cost model (rules-based) + console modal UX + CLI stub.
- Week 4: integration test with small-sample live probes for 3 models; collect error stats vs actual calls.
- Week 5–6: add suggestions engine and basic mapping to Optimize recommendations.
- Week 7–8: dogfood with 3 internal teams, gather feedback, refine UX and thresholds.

Example scenarios to include in docs (dev-friendly)
- "Chat reply" short (input 120 tokens, expected output 60) — guidance: use small model, streaming off, estimated saving 3x vs default.
- "Summarization" long (input 3000, output 200) — guidance: use streaming, consider chunked summarization + rerank to reduce end-to-end compute.
- "Rerank pipeline" (n=16 candidates) — guidance: use embeddings-first filter, reduce n for first pass; show candidate-cost tradeoff.

Next actions (for me)
- Mock up Console modal and CLI args; post to #product-optimize for early feedback.
- Request billing pricing matrix and per-model calibration traces.
- Schedule 30m sync with Optimize eng and Console PM.

Notes-to-self (short):
- Keep the tool lightweight and honest (confidence bands).
- Default to conservative estimates for hosted customers; show cheaper options but mark as lower fidelity.
- Don't bake in billing logic for Dedicated/Private until we have mapping table.

End of notes.

(Informal, rough — intended as a personal scratch document to iterate into a PRD/one-pager.)
